analysis.title: The Crash Before The Crash: Memory Stocks Implode As AI Credit Stress Explodes
key_insights: Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron have fallen an average 42% from recent peaks per JPMorgan, versus an average drawdown of about 49% across the previous four major memory downcycles.
JPMorgan sees little evidence that a memory downcycle has begun. Its three classic warning signals (weakening prices, rising inventories, deteriorating orders) are largely missing.
DDR4/DDR5 spot prices remain firm, inventories are exceptionally tight, and order discussions extend into 2028-2029.
Korea is being sold heavily. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate the index, so selling Korea is effectively selling the memory trade (GS chart).
Micron reported data-center revenue above $34bn in its latest fiscal quarter, with Cloud Memory revenue up 258% y/y and Core Data Center revenue up 1,024% y/y, per JPMorgan's credit team.
Over 75% of Micron's FY27 shipments are already committed, with allocation discussions extending into 2028. HBM demand is strong and supply constraints limit availability.

JPMorgan highlights NVIDIA's involvement in a $500bn AI financing platform, including residual value guarantees on certain transactions. Broadcom is increasingly involved in large-scale customer financing.
Broadcom's 2041 bond spread has widened 94bp YTD and NVIDIA's 2040 bond has widened 71bp despite accelerating AI earnings.
JPMorgan remains constructive on semiconductor fundamentals but is increasingly selective on credit because of financing commitments and potential contingent liabilities.

CoreWeave's sell-off has intensified scrutiny of debt-funded AI infrastructure. JPMorgan does not see restructuring as its base case, but tighter financing could delay deployments and eventually hit chip orders.
The market appears to be discounting a memory earnings peak as early as 1H 2027. Samsung and SK Hynix trade at 2-3x estimated 2027/2028 earnings and about 0.9-1.5x forward price-to-book (GS).

JPMorgan lists possible sentiment catalysts: stronger HBM demand, continued supply discipline, new AI applications and more aggressive shareholder returns including buybacks. Next earnings commentary on 2027 pricing, committed HBM supply and capex discipline is key.

SK Hynix and Samsung are approaching major long-term trendlines, trade below their 200-day moving averages and show deeply oversold momentum. Micron has held up better, remains within its multi-month range and above its 200-day average, with oversold momentum.

The Market Ear sees potential for a sharp counter-trend rally but says a tradable bounce is not necessarily a durable bottom. Credit stabilization and improving relative strength are needed as confirmation.

market_movers.rationale: Over 75% of FY27 shipments are committed and data-center revenue exceeded $34bn in the latest fiscal quarter. The stock has held up better than Korean peers and momentum is oversold.
The 2040 bond spread has widened 71bp YTD on the company's involvement in a $500bn AI financing platform with residual value guarantees.
The 2041 bond spread has widened 94bp YTD as the company takes part in large-scale customer financing arrangements.
The recent sell-off has increased scrutiny of its dependence on external financing and on NVIDIA as GPU supplier, equity investor and capacity purchaser.

sector_views.rationale: JPMorgan sees no downcycle signals in prices, inventories or orders while the stocks are down about 42%. The Market Ear sees a possible bounce but wants credit and relative-strength confirmation.

earnings_insights: Micron reported data-center revenue above $34bn in its latest fiscal quarter, with Cloud Memory revenue +258% y/y and Core Data Center revenue +1,024% y/y (reported, per JPMorgan credit team).
Samsung and SK Hynix trade at 2-3x estimated 2027/2028 earnings (estimates, per GS). Next earnings updates will be watched for 2027 pricing, committed HBM supply and capex discipline.
risk_factors: Tighter AI financing conditions could delay deployments and eventually reduce semiconductor orders.
NVIDIA's residual value guarantees and Broadcom's customer financing create potential contingent liabilities.
CoreWeave's dependence on external financing, and NVIDIA's multiple exposures to it as supplier, equity investor and contracted capacity purchaser.
The market may be correctly anticipating a sharp memory earnings reversal after a peak in 1H 2027.
A counter-trend bounce may not be a durable bottom without credit stabilization.
vol_and_positioning: Investors are selling Korea heavily, and because Samsung and SK Hynix dominate the index this is effectively selling the memory trade.
Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron are down an average 42% from peaks, close to the 49% average drawdown of the previous four downcycles.
SK Hynix and Samsung trade below their 200-day moving averages with deeply oversold momentum. Micron's momentum is also deeply oversold but its 200-day average is well below the current price.
cross_bank_references: JPMorgan and GS are the sources cited for the charts and data in this note.

tension_points.bull_case: Memory prices are firm, inventories tight, and orders extend into 2028-2029. Over 75% of Micron FY27 shipments are committed. Stocks are down about 42% and trade at 2-3x 2027/2028 earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: The market may be discounting a memory earnings peak in 1H 2027. AI financing stress, including widening NVIDIA and Broadcom spreads and CoreWeave's sell-off, could delay deployments and cut chip orders.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A bounce is not a durable bottom without credit stabilization and improving relative strength.
